name: Solenne Atelier Ossuary Couture Veil Coat
description: A singular piece by Solenne Atelier's lead designer Ifeoma Vasić-Nakamura, constructed over eight months from cultured bone-lace panels grown in a biolab and laser-cut into interlocking geometric screens. The silhouette is an oversized cocoon coat that falls to the ankle, the bone-lace layered over a base of liquid-black nanosilk that shifts between opacity and translucency based on ambient temperature. The collar rises into a structured halo frame supporting a detachable veil of graphene-mesh so fine it reads as smoke. Wrist closures are hand-set with reclaimed antique jet beads from pre-Collapse Edo-era jewelry. One of three made.
functionality: Nanosilk layer provides passive thermal regulation. Graphene veil filters 40% of particulate air pollution. Bone-lace panels are structurally reinforced — surprisingly impact-resistant for haute couture.
what_it_says: This person exists at a level where clothing is no longer about function or even status — it is about authorship.
worn_by: one known to be owned by a sitting Crucible board member
story_hooks: One of the three coats has gone missing from a private auction — the designer is quietly frantic, the buyer is not yet aware.
A journalist discovers the 'cultured bone-lace' was grown from genetic material sourced without consent from Shelf-tier residents used in a biolab study.
Wearing this coat to a particular Spire gathering is understood as a declaration of alliance with a specific corponation faction — the wearer may not know this.
